title: Pointed common refinements of affine SNC stratum charts
statement: Let $k$ be a field, $Y$ a regular separated finite-type $k$-scheme [def-weil-regular-scheme], $D=\bigcup_{a\in A}D_a$ a finite labelled strict normal crossings boundary [def-trf-strict-normal-crossings-boundary], and $I\subseteq A$. Put $Y_I=Y\setminus\bigcup_{a\notin I}D_a$ and let $S$ be the reduced intersection of the $D_i$, $i\in I$, in $Y_I$. Fix $s:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to S$ [def-weil-geometric-point]. For each of finitely many indices $a$, let $V_a=\operatorname{Spec}B_a\to Y_I$ be affine etale [def-weil-etale-morphism], with a lift of $s$, labelled equations $t_{a,i}\in B_a$, $i\in I$, where $t_{a,i}$ generates the ideal of the closed subscheme $V_a\times_{Y}D_i$ of $V_a$, having the regular-parameter property at every point [def-weil-pbc-regular-system-of-parameters], and nonempty connected regular residual scheme $\operatorname{Spec}(B_a/J_a)$, $J_a=(t_{a,i})$. There is an affine etale chart $W=\operatorname{Spec}B\to Y_I$ of the same type (its equations $t_i$ generate the ideals of the $W\times_YD_i$), with a lift of $s$, and pointed etale maps $W\to V_a$ over $Y_I$. The maps $B_a\to B$ carry $J_a$ onto the ideal $J=(t_i)$ after extension, and induce compatible maps $B_a^h\to B^h$ on pair henselizations [lem-weil-pbc-pair-henselization]. For the pointed universal covers [lem-sfb-pointed-finite-etale-limit-cover] of these henselizations and of their residual schemes, the induced maps on their rings $H_a\to H$ and $H_a/J_aH_a\to H/JH$ commute with the base, henselization, and reduction maps. These maps compose under further pointed refinements, using the canonical identifications of the cover systems.

source.place: 0A02 (lemma-henselization), universal property; pione.tex 09ZS (lemma-gabber); ILO VIII Remark 4.2.2(i), p.118, and naturality of the pointed finite-etale limit cover. Agent fibre-product and affine-component refinement.

proof.text: First all the given $B_a$ are Noetherian. Indeed $Y_I$ is locally Noetherian by regularity and restriction to an open. An etale map is locally of finite presentation, hence locally of finite type (a finite presentation supplies finitely many generators), so local Noetherianity ascends to $V_a$; its affine coordinate ring is Noetherian. Independently choose one reference affine open $V_0=\operatorname{Spec}B_0\subseteq Y_I$ from the labelled affine stratum charts, containing the image of $s$. The geometric point factors through this open. The reference chart has globally labelled equations $t_{0,i}$, regular Noetherian coordinate ring and nonempty connected regular residual scheme. This extra reference is also available when the given finite family is empty.

source.place: Tag 01T6 (lemma-finite-type-noetherian); ILO VIII Remark 4.2.2(i), p.118, via the labelled affine chart lemma.

proof.text: Starting with $P_0=V_0$, enumerate the finitely many given charts and set $P_{j+1}=P_j\times_{Y_I}V_{a_j}$. The universal property supplies the point $s_{j+1}$ from the two lifts of $s$. Inductively the projections and structure maps are etale: the new projections are base changes of etale maps and their composites are etale. Choose an affine open $X=\operatorname{Spec}C$ containing the resulting point. Its maps to $V_0$, all $V_a$ and $Y_I$ are etale, since an open immersion is etale. Pull the $t_{0,i}$ back to $c_i\in C$. The etale-coordinate parameter theorem, including its $r=0$ case, makes $X$ regular locally Noetherian and preserves the vanishing parameter subtuple at every point; thus $C$ is Noetherian. For $I\ne\varnothing$, the coordinate-intersection theorem makes $R=\operatorname{Spec}(C/(c_i))$ regular and reduced, and identifies it scheme-theoretically with the intersection of all the pulled-back $D_i$. For $I=\varnothing$ put $R=X$. The point lies on $R$ in both cases.

source.place: Tags 07QP (lemma-dimension-etale-extension), 0AH0 (lemma-regular-etale-extension); schemes.tex 01IT (lemma-basis-affine-opens); agent finite fibre-product induction.

proof.text: The quotient $C/(c_i)$ is Noetherian: an ascending chain of its ideals pulls back to an ascending chain of ideals of $C$. Its spectrum $R$ is therefore a Noetherian space. Let $K$ be the connected component through the marked point; it is open by the Noetherian component theorem and closed: the closure of a connected set is connected (a separation of the closure by two relative opens would restrict to a separation of the dense set), so maximality of the component forces it to equal its closure. Choose its idempotent $e\in C/(c_i)$ and lift $e$ to $f\in C$. Set $B=C_f$, $W=\operatorname{Spec}B$ and $t_i=c_i/1$. The principal-open theorem identifies $W=D(f)\subseteq X$; the point factors through it since $e$ has value $1$ at that point. Localizing the quotient gives $B/(t_i)=(C/(c_i))_e$, whose spectrum is exactly $K$. Thus the residual scheme is nonempty connected and regular. Restriction preserves the labelled equations and their parameter property, so $W$ is the required chart, with the pointed etale maps of step 2. This also handles $I=\varnothing$ without introducing a nonexistent parameter.

source.place: Tag 00EE (lemma-disjoint-decomposition); topology.tex 04MF (lemma-locally-Noetherian-locally-connected), 04ME (lemma-locally-connected). Agent lift of the residual idempotent; quotient/localization identity from their universal properties.

proof.text: Write $\varphi_a:B_a\to B$ for a chart map. For every label $i$, both $\varphi_a(t_{a,i})$ and $t_i$ generate the ideal of the same closed subscheme $W\times_YD_i$: this is the defining pullback of its ideal and the specified labelled equations. Summing these equal ideals gives $J_aB=J$. In particular $\varphi_a$ induces $\bar\varphi_a:B_a/J_a\to B/J$, carrying the residual marked point to the prescribed one. Apply pair henselization to all these pairs; the structure maps identify each residue quotient with the original one and make the target pair henselian. Apply the henselization universal property to $B_a\to B\to B^h$ and $(B^h,JB^h)$. It gives the unique extension $\varphi_a^h:B_a^h\to B^h$. Its reduction is $\bar\varphi_a$ because both maps agree after the surjective quotient map from $B_a$.

source.place: Tag 0A02 (lemma-henselization), residual quotient and last paragraph (adjunction). Labelled-ideal equality is elementary pullback of the specified ideals.

proof.text: Apply the henselian pointed-residual-cover lift theorem to $(B_a,J_a)$ and $(B,J)$: Noetherianity was checked in steps 1--3 and the residual schemes are nonempty connected. Put $E_a=B_a^h$, $E=B^h$. The theorem supplies connected affine bases $\operatorname{Spec}E_a$, $\operatorname{Spec}E$, their pointed universal covers $T_a=\operatorname{Spec}H_a$, $T=\operatorname{Spec}H$, and identifies $\operatorname{Spec}(H_a/J_aH_a)$ and $\operatorname{Spec}(H/JH)$ as the residual pointed universal covers. All these bases are qcqs since they are affine. Apply pointed-limit functoriality to $\operatorname{Spec}E\to\operatorname{Spec}E_a$ induced by $\varphi_a^h$. Its marked points are compatible by the reduction calculation in step 4. We get the pointed map $F_a:T\to T_a$, hence $\Phi_a:H_a\to H$, with $\Phi_a\eta_{H_a/E_a}=\eta_{H/E}\varphi_a^h$. Composing with $B_a\to E_a$ proves the required base and henselization squares.

source.place: Tag 09ZS (lemma-gabber) and Tag 0BND (theorem-fundamental-group), (1),(3); agent application of the existing pointed-limit naturality statement.

proof.text: Since $\Phi_a$ extends $\varphi_a$, it sends $J_aH_a$ into $JH$, and therefore induces $\bar\Phi_a:H_a/J_aH_a\to H/JH$ with $q\Phi_a=\bar\Phi_a q_a$. This is precisely the pointed universal-cover map for $\operatorname{Spec}(B/J)\to\operatorname{Spec}(B_a/J_a)$: the quotient morphism of covers is pointed and lies over this residual map, and uniqueness in pointed-limit functoriality identifies it with that map. This uses the actual residual-cover identifications from step 5, not merely an equivalence of finite cover objects. Under a further pointed refinement $W'\to W$, the two candidate extensions $B_a^h\to (B')^h$ agree by the henselization universal property, since they extend the same map on $B_a$. The two maps from the universal cover over $W'$ to $T_a$ agree by pointed-limit uniqueness. Passing to rings and then their quotients proves composition and all reduction squares. Finally these same uniqueness assertions identify different cofinal cover systems by inverse pointed maps and make the identifications commute with every refinement. Thus the asserted compatibility is independent of the presentation of each pointed cover system.

source.place: Tag 0BND (theorem-fundamental-group), (3); more-algebra.tex Tag 0A02 (lemma-henselization). Agent quotient calculation and uniqueness assembly.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q76-8dbca438b (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read the item and all 20 cited statements; there are no new nodes and the statement is unchanged. The six steps hold. (1) B_a is Noetherian by regularity, étale is locally of finite type, and the locally Noetherian and affine-open lemmas apply. The reference chart V_0 comes from labelled-affine-stratum-charts, whose hypotheses match exactly, so the case of zero given charts is covered. (2) A pointed iterated fibre product over Y_I, with étaleness by base change and composition and an affine open X=Spec C. trf divisor-parameters, with U=V_0 and z=t_{0,i}, gives regularity and parameter transport; trf intersection-geometry, for I nonempty, gives V(c_i) as the scheme-theoretic intersection of the pulled-back D_i, regular and reduced. (3) The Noetherian quotient gives an open component, closedness is proved, and the clopen component gives an idempotent e. Its lift f is not treated as idempotent (E4 avoided), and B=C_f has residual (C/(c_i))_e equal to the component through the point.
